podcast.title: "Suzy Q" Guitar Riff Architect
podcast.body: James Burton was the guitarist who created the distinctive, biting guitar riff for Dale Hawkins' "Suzy Q," playing on both the demo and the final released version. Despite his crucial contribution, he controversially received no songwriting credit. "But everyone seems agreed that Hawkins came up with the lyrics while Burton came up with the guitar riff."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Post-Hawkins Session Career
podcast.body: After leaving Dale Hawkins' band, James Burton went on to work with Louisiana musician Bob Luman, then Ricky Nelson, and became a highly sought-after session player, contributing to recordings for artists ranging from The Monkees to Elvis Presley. "Burton then went on to work, first with Vicki Nelson, and then as a session player with everyone from the monkeys to Elvis."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Reunion with Hawkins
podcast.body: Burton reunited with Dale Hawkins in the late 1960s to play guitar on Hawkins' Swamp Rock-style album. This comeback was prompted by Creedence Clearwater Revival's successful cover of "Suzy Q." "working once again with James Burton on guitar"

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
